@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+"""cycle-127 FR-3.4 guard (SDD D-3.4): the suites whose Opus 5.5 ceiling pins
+were swept to read the catalog must not grow a literal 180K back.
+
+The uncalibrated policy cap (`CEILING_CAP = 180_000`, the 4.x/5-family
+entries' bound until a probe calibrates them) is the one literal allowed, and
+it is allowed only as that named constant and in its SDD §2.1 docstring. Every
+other `180000` / `180_000` / `180,000` in these files fails this test — a
+literal there would turn red when the probe writes the measured Opus 5.5 bound.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+LITERAL = re.compile(r"(?<![\d_,])180[_,]?000(?![\d_,])")
+
+# file → the exact lines allowed to carry the literal (the policy cap, not the Opus 5.5 value)
+SWEPT = {
+    ".claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py": {
+        "CEILING_CAP = 180_000",
+        '"""SDD §2.1: ceiling = min(180000, context_window − default_max_tokens(entry)) — computed, not a constant."""',
+    },
+    "tests/unit/loa-status-providers.bats": set(),
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rel", sorted(SWEPT))
+def test_no_literal_opus_5_5_ceiling_in_a_swept_suite(rel):
+    path = ROOT / rel
+    assert path.is_file(), rel
+    offenders = [
+        f"{rel}:{n}: {line.strip()}"
+        for n, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1)
+        if LITERAL.search(line) and line.strip() not in SWEPT[rel]
+    ]
+    assert offenders == [], "read the catalog instead of pinning the Opus 5.5 bound:\n" + "\n".join(offenders)
+
+
+def test_the_policy_cap_is_never_compared_against_the_opus_5_5_entry_directly():
+    text = (ROOT / ".claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py").read_text()
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        if "CEILING_CAP" in line and "claude-opus-5-5" in line:
+            pytest.fail(f"CEILING_CAP pinned against claude-opus-5-5: {line.strip()}")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("line, hit", [
+    ("x == 180000", True), ("x == 180_000", True), ("probed 180,000 tokens", True),
+    ("1800000000", False), ("180_000_000", False), ("1180000", False), ("18000", False),
+])
+def test_the_guard_pattern(line, hit):
+    assert bool(LITERAL.search(line)) is hit

+"""cycle-127 FR-3.4 guard (SDD D-3.4): the suites whose Opus 5.5 ceiling pins
+were swept to read the catalog must not grow a literal 180K back.
+
+The uncalibrated policy cap (`CEILING_CAP = 180_000`, the 4.x/5-family
+entries' bound until a probe calibrates them) is the one literal allowed, and
+it is allowed only as that named constant and in its SDD §2.1 docstring. Every
+other `180000` / `180_000` / `180,000` in these files fails this test — a
+literal there would turn red when the probe writes the measured Opus 5.5 bound.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+LITERAL = re.compile(r"(?<![\d_,])180[_,]?000(?![\d_,])")
+
+# file → the exact lines allowed to carry the literal (the policy cap, not the Opus 5.5 value)
+SWEPT = {
+    ".claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py": {
+        "CEILING_CAP = 180_000",
+        '"""SDD §2.1: ceiling = min(180000, context_window − default_max_tokens(entry)) — computed, not a constant."""',
+    },
+    "tests/unit/loa-status-providers.bats": set(),
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rel", sorted(SWEPT))
+def test_no_literal_opus_5_5_ceiling_in_a_swept_suite(rel):
+    path = ROOT / rel
+    assert path.is_file(), rel
+    offenders = [
+        f"{rel}:{n}: {line.strip()}"
+        for n, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1)
+        if LITERAL.search(line) and line.strip() not in SWEPT[rel]
+    ]
+    assert offenders == [], "read the catalog instead of pinning the Opus 5.5 bound:\n" + "\n".join(offenders)
+
+
+def test_the_policy_cap_is_never_compared_against_the_opus_5_5_entry_directly():
+    text = (ROOT / ".claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py").read_text()
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        if "CEILING_CAP" in line and "claude-opus-5-5" in line:
+            pytest.fail(f"CEILING_CAP pinned against claude-opus-5-5: {line.strip()}")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("line, hit", [
+    ("x == 180000", True), ("x == 180_000", True), ("probed 180,000 tokens", True),
+    ("1800000000", False), ("180_000_000", False), ("1180000", False), ("18000", False),
+])
+def test_the_guard_pattern(line, hit):
+    assert bool(LITERAL.search(line)) is hit

+++ b/.claude/adapters/tests/test_no_literal_opus55_ceiling_pins.py
@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+"""cycle-127 FR-3.4 guard (SDD D-3.4): the suites whose Opus 5.5 ceiling pins
+were swept to read the catalog must not grow a literal 180K back.
+
+The uncalibrated policy cap (`CEILING_CAP = 180_000`, the 4.x/5-family
+entries' bound until a probe calibrates them) is the one literal allowed, and
+it is allowed only as that named constant and in its SDD §2.1 docstring. Every
+other `180000` / `180_000` / `180,000` in these files fails this test — a
+literal there would turn red when the probe writes the measured Opus 5.5 bound.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+LITERAL = re.compile(r"(?<![\d_,])180[_,]?000(?![\d_,])")
+
+# file → the exact lines allowed to carry the literal (the policy cap, not the Opus 5.5 value)
+SWEPT = {
+    ".claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py": {
+        "CEILING_CAP = 180_000",
+        '"""SDD §2.1: ceiling = min(180000, context_window − default_max_tokens(entry)) — computed, not a constant."""',
+    },
+    "tests/unit/loa-status-providers.bats": set(),
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rel", sorted(SWEPT))
+def test_no_literal_opus_5_5_ceiling_in_a_swept_suite(rel):
+    path = ROOT / rel
+    assert path.is_file(), rel
+    offenders = [
+        f"{rel}:{n}: {line.strip()}"
+        for n, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1)
+        if LITERAL.search(line) and line.strip() not in SWEPT[rel]
+    ]
+    assert offenders == [], "read the catalog instead of pinning the Opus 5.5 bound:\n" + "\n".join(offenders)
+
+
+def test_the_policy_cap_is_never_compared_against_the_opus_5_5_entry_directly():
+    text = (ROOT / ".claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py").read_text()
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        if "CEILING_CAP" in line and "claude-opus-5-5" in line:
+            pytest.fail(f"CEILING_CAP pinned against claude-opus-5-5: {line.strip()}")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("line, hit", [
+    ("x == 180000", True), ("x == 180_000", True), ("probed 180,000 tokens", True),
+    ("1800000000", False), ("180_000_000", False), ("1180000", False), ("18000", False),
+])
+def test_the_guard_pattern(line, hit):
+    assert bool(LITERAL.search(line)) is hit

+    above a rejection."""
+    reasons: list[str] = []
+    if stop == "budget":

+    if stop == "other" or any(s.get("kind") == "other" for s in samples):
+        reasons.append("an attempt failed for a non-size reason (other)")
+    if stop == "unverified" or any(s.get("kind") == "unverified" for s in samples):
+        reasons.append("a completed response did not echo the needle (unverified)")
+    oks = [s.get("size_measured", s["tokens"]) for s in samples if s.get("kind") == "ok"]
+    fails = [s.get("size_measured", s["tokens"]) for s in samples if s.get("kind") == "size"]

+def _outcome_reasons(samples: list[dict], *, stop: str | None, largest_ok: int, measured: int | None,
+                     smallest_fail: int | None, hi: int, tol: int) -> list[str]:
+    """Why a bisection is NOT clean ([] ⇒ clean; sprint.md § Flatline review integration (a)):
+    clean = the largest accepted step verified by the echoed needle and measured, a size
+    rejection within `tol` above it, no `other` / unverified / budget stop, no accept
+    above a rejection."""
+    reasons: list[str] = []
+    if stop == "budget":
+        reasons.append("budget cap stopped the bisection")
+    if stop == "other" or any(s.get("kind") == "other" for s in samples):
+        reasons.append("an attempt failed for a non-size reason (other)")
+    if stop == "unverified" or any(s.get("kind") == "unverified" for s in samples):
+        reasons.append("a completed response did not echo the needle (unverified)")
+    oks = [s.get("size_measured", s["tokens"]) for s in samples if s.get("kind") == "ok"]
+    fails = [s.get("size_measured", s["tokens"]) for s in samples if s.get("kind") == "size"]
+    if oks and fails and max(oks) > min(fails):
+        reasons.append("inconsistent: an accept above a size rejection")
+    if reasons:
+        return reasons
+    if largest_ok <= 0:
+        reasons.append("no accepted size in the probed range")
+    elif smallest_fail is None or (largest_ok >= hi - tol and smallest_fail - largest_ok > tol):
+        reasons.append(f"no size rejection up to {hi} tokens — the bound is not bracketed")
+    elif smallest_fail - largest_ok > tol:
+        reasons.append("the accept/reject bracket is wider than --tolerance-tokens")
+    elif not measured:
+        reasons.append("the accepted step reported no usage — nothing measured")
+    return reasons

+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

+setup() {

+    local opt t

+        for opt in absent false '"true"'; do
+            _cfg "$t" "$opt"
+            [ "$(get_model_tertiary)" = "" ] || { echo "t=$t opt=$opt planned"; return 1; }
+            [ "$(get_tertiary_status)" = "disabled_by_opt_in" ]
+            run tertiary_opt_in_skip_reason
+            [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

+    ! grep -q gemini-headless "$CALLS" || { echo "unexpected: grep -q gemini-headless '$CALLS'"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(grep -c '' "$CALLS")" = "4" ]

+    [[ "$stderr" != *"Voice dropped"* ]]
+}

Outcome `clean` = the largest accepted step is verified, a size rejection
sits within --tolerance-tokens above it, and nothing was `other`,
unverified, budget-capped or inconsistent; anything else is `partial`
(exit 3; exit 1 when an `other` failure stopped it). The record is always
written; only `clean` with `--write-catalog` touches the catalog:
`probed_ceiling` and `effective_input_ceiling` = the measured accepted size
(raw — the api transport applies no safety margin either; a bound below
180K is written as measured, never kept) and `ceiling_calibration`
{source: operator_set, method: probed_headless, transport, cli_version,
cli_model, measured_input_tokens, …}.
  `reprobe_trigger` naming the API-transport probe. The record is always written. Use it
  on hosts where the direct API is unreachable (this repo's primary host: KF-040) and the
  CLI route is what your hops actually use; `--transport api` is unchanged.
- **`claude-opus-5-5` input bound: 180,000 → 936,000 on this route.** Measured 2026-10-07
  through `claude-bedrock` (`global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`, CLI 2.1.292): accepted and
  verified at 972,887 input tokens, rejected by the CLI's pre-flight at the 1,000,000 window;
  written as 936,000 = 1,000,000 − the 64,000 default output budget (cheval's I2 invariant),
  `ceiling_calibration.source: operator_set`, `method: probed_headless`,
  `measured_input_tokens: 972887`. cheval now preempts above 936,000 instead of 180,000 for
  `opus`, and Bridgebuilder's budget for it is 916,000 input tokens. Record:
  `grimoires/loa/reports/2026-10-07-opus-5-5-ceiling-probe-cli.json`. Downstream mounts
  inherit the value with the catalog; re-probe through your own route if it differs.

head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:494 — The `claude-opus-5-5` HTTP-API entry (`auth_type: http_api`) has its `effective_input_ceiling` raised from 180000 to 936000 based on one probe run through claude-headless on Bedrock. That run ended `partial`: the budget cap stopped it, and the bracket from the 972,887 accept to the ~1,065,182 rejection is far wider than the 16K tolerance. The tool written in this same PR refuses to write the catalog on a `partial` outcome, so the value was hand-entered as `operator_set`, getting past the tool's own evidence gate. The direct-API route was never probed (the `reprobe_trigger` says so), yet cheval's preempt threshold for every `opus` HTTP call, every downstream mount, and the Bridgebuilder budget all move about 5×. Keep the conservative bound on the API entry until a clean probe of that route exists, or scope the measured bound to the route that was actually measured.
head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:502 — `probed_ceiling: 936000` records a value that was never probed or accepted as a clean bound. It is the I2-clamped figure from a partial run. `test_anthropic_catalog_floor._measured()` and LSP-5 then treat any `operator_set` entry with `calibrated_at` as measured, so the 180K policy guard stops applying to this entry.
head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/agy_headless_adapter.py:125 — `AgyOptInRequiredError` is a `ConfigError`/`ChevalError`, and cheval's chain walk hard-aborts on it (`except ChevalError` → return). It does not skip the hop. Under `hounfour.headless.mode: prefer-cli`, `gemini-headless` is the first hop of every Google chain, so with the default-off gate every Google voice now fails INVALID_CONFIG before its HTTP hops are tried. Under prefer-api the terminal refusal replaces the real (often retryable) cause of the earlier hop failures with a non-retryable INVALID_CONFIG. An opt-in gate on one hop should be a walkable, not-planned skip inside the chain walk, not a hard abort of the whole invocation.
head/.claude/scripts/flatline-orchestrator.sh:534 — `_tertiary_routes_to_agy` treats a Google model as agy-routed only under `cli-only`. Under `prefer-cli`, cheval puts the `gemini-headless` CLI hop first, and that hop now hard-aborts with opt_in_required. So the tertiary is planned, dispatched, and fails as a degraded voice: the exact outcome FR-1 is meant to remove.
head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:182 — `isAgyRouted` has the same gap: only `cli-only` counts as agy-routed. Under `prefer-cli` a Google voice is planned, cheval refuses it at the first (agy) hop, and the review drops to DEGRADED 2/3, which is the #1274 symptom this PR says it fixes. The compiled `dist/config.js` carries the same logic.
head/.claude/scripts/run-preflight.sh:190 — P3 gates only a literal `gemini-headless` hop (`cli_for`). A Google model under `cli-only`/`prefer-cli`, which cheval routes through agy, still counts as a usable voice whenever GOOGLE_API_KEY is present. Flatline and Bridgebuilder each define a different agy-routing predicate, so the planners disagree about which voices are planned.
head/docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md:305 — The migration note describes the 936,000 bound as measured, with the rejection "at the 1,000,000 window". It does not say that the probe outcome was `partial` (budget-capped, bracket not closed), or that the rejection was observed at ~1,065,182. Two bullets earlier (line 296) it says the tool writes the catalog only on a clean outcome, so downstream operators are misled about how strong the evidence behind the new bound is.
head/tools/ceiling-probe-live.py:44 — The module docstring still says the CLI transport writes the measured accepted size "raw". After the fr23b fix, `write_catalog_operator_set` writes `min(measured, context_window − default_max_tokens)` through `i2_clamped`, so the usage text contradicts the behaviour.
head/tools/ceiling-probe-live.py:363 — `--allow-partial` is silently ignored on the `claude-headless` transport: `_main_cli` never reads it and returns 3 without writing. The flag should either be rejected for this transport or documented as api-only.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
My verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**, and the review is in `/workspace/review.md`: nine findings, then the verdict line. I worked from reading the diff only. I ran none of the tests, because `pr/head/` holds just the touched files and can't run on its own.

What blocks the merge:

1. **The Opus 5.5 input limit is raised on weak evidence** (`model-config.yaml:494`, `:502`). The entry used for direct API calls goes from 180,000 to 936,000 tokens. That number comes from a single probe run through the command-line tool on Bedrock, not through the direct API. The run ended `partial`: the budget cap stopped it before the limit was pinned down. The probe tool added in this same PR refuses to write the catalog after a partial run, so the value was entered by hand. The direct API route was never probed. The migration doc also leaves out that the run was partial (`docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md:305`).
2. **Turning agy off can break Google voices entirely** (`agy_headless_adapter.py:125`). When the opt-in is off, the agy adapter raises a config error. Cheval stops the whole call on that error instead of skipping to the next option in the fallback chain. In `prefer-cli` mode agy is the first option in every Google chain, so with the new default every Google call fails before the regular Google API is tried. In the default `prefer-api` mode, the refusal at the end of the chain hides the real (often retryable) error from the earlier attempts.
3. **The planners don't recognise that case.** Flatline (`flatline-orchestrator.sh:534`) and Bridgebuilder (`config.ts:182`) only treat a Google model as going through agy in `cli-only` mode. Under `prefer-cli` they still plan the Google voice, cheval then refuses it, and the review comes out degraded at 2 of 3 voices. That is the #1274 symptom this PR says it fixes. The run preflight check (`run-preflight.sh:190`) uses a third, different rule for the same question.

Smaller issues:
- The probe tool's description (`tools/ceiling-probe-live.py:44`) still says it writes the raw measured size, but it now caps the value so input plus the default output fits in the model's context window.
- `--allow-partial` is silently ignored when the probe runs through the command-line tool (`tools/ceiling-probe-live.py:512`).

The rest looked correct: how the opt-in is read (only a real YAML `true` counts, with no environment override), the new effort-default logic in cheval, the schema additions, and the status display.
